answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut is mandatory and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms cannot meet the mandate. The primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, forcing a decision now. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone, and I want to verify memory_c2 (the archived record of last year's switch) before committing, because it bears directly on onboarding speed, delivery reliability, and invoicing accuracy—the delivery-risk factors that matter with the assembly line at 94% and no buffer. memory_c1 (incumbent renewal kept integration stable) is noted, but the incumbent has removed itself as a viable cost option. memory_c5's deferral pattern is inapplicable because the contract does not auto-renew; there is no month-to-month fallback. Choosing switch_primary_vendor as the single decision this cycle; add_second_source would preserve redundancy but does not address the mandated cost reduction within the one-action constraint. Accept the delivery risk of a new primary vendor rather than breach the cost mandate, pending verification of memory_c2's onboarding record.
